summary: B is narrowly preferable because it better preserves existing Files option semantics and handles seek failures more compatibly, though neither patch satisfies the frozen contract closely enough to merge unchanged.
reasons: B allows both WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions to affect Upload and forwards the query; A's separate FilesUploadOption excludes WithFilesQuery and therefore loses existing FilesOption behavior.

B's replay helper falls back to the previous one-shot behavior when an io.Seeker cannot report its position. A instead fails the request before sending it, creating a concrete compatibility regression for partially seekable readers such as pipes.
B has stronger tests around caller ownership of seekable readers and the unchanged single-attempt behavior of non-seekable bodies.
Both implementations correctly create a replayable multipart body and validate the required filename and content arguments, so the differentiators above are meaningful.
risks_a: Upload has opts ...FilesUploadOption rather than the required opts ...FilesOption.
Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and calls Raw.Do directly, duplicating request, decoding, and error logic.

It adds prohibited association options and NewFileWithFields machinery instead of calling multipartbody.NewFile directly, while also changing global retry behavior and Update behavior through Raw.DoFwrap? No—Raw.Do changes affect Update globally by making seekable bodies replayable and changing ownership semantics. Does not alter Update code itself except docs. Need not typo. Let's formulate cleanly.
risks_b: Upload has opts ...UploadFileOption rather than the required opts ...FilesOption and bypasses FilesService.Add.
It adds prohibited association and arbitrary multipart-field APIs, and changes the static return types of existing option constructors.

It modifies global request/retry ownership behavior despite the contract explicitly limiting scope to Upload; GetBody also reuses a single mutable seeker rather than producing an independent body reader.
